expected: the Jevellan web app "undo" screen at desktop-light, rendered completely and legibly (one of several screens captured during "step corrections survive reload and undo launches the requested redo with visible history"; the other steps are judged in their own screenshots)

cosmetic: Conversation titles and subtitles in the sidebar are cut off with ellipses (e.g. 'Change the value to thre…', 'Context · J11 memory journ…'). This is normal sidebar overflow, and the selected item is still identifiable.
The undone Step 1 is struck through, its code blocks are greyed out (grey background), and its label text is faint. This marks it as undone on purpose. The text is lighter but still readable.
The two red error banners repeat the word 'disabled' eight times ('No model can run this step right now: disabled, disabled, …'). This is a wording/content issue, not a layout problem.
The 'Step details' disclosure rows and the small labels such as 'Local time' and 'completed' are low-contrast grey but still readable.
